profile.reading: This is T-Mobile Polskas data processing center on ul. Szlachecka in Warsaw, Poland, built under a contract signed with Austrian construction firm STRABAG on July 8, 2020, originally scheduled for completion in September 2021 and launched into service in December 2021. The building sits on an 8,529 square meter site with a total building footprint of about 6,400 square meters, or roughly 68,900 square feet, and roughly 4,380 to 4,400 square meters, or about 47,100 square feet, of usable floor area across three above ground floors of reinforced concrete monolithic construction, combining office and technical space. At launch, T-Mobile described more than 1,700 square meters of dedicated colocation space within the building, with an initial financial sector client occupying about 250 square meters of it. The facility was built to ANSI/TIA-942 Rated-3 standards, providing full redundancy across its architectural, mechanical, climate, ventilation, energy, and telecommunications systems, also cited as meeting EN-PN 50600 European data center standards, targeting a power usage effectiveness of about 1.3 and running on a claimed 100 percent renewable electricity supply, with 400 gigabit per second Ethernet interconnection linking it to T-Mobile Polskas other facilities. Polish construction trade press described it at the time as one of the most modern data center facilities in Poland, supporting colocation, hosting, private cloud and virtual data center services, backup and disaster recovery as a service, VPN, and cybersecurity offerings, with T-Mobile stating it operates roughly 15 data centers across Poland in total providing georedundant disaster recovery across multiple sites. T-Mobile Polska is the Polish operating subsidiary of Germanys Deutsche Telekom group. Deutsche Telekom holds a majority stake in T-Mobile Polska.
